text:
leo_support: incoming escalation from Acme Corp. embeddings endpoint returning "dimension mismatch" when they call via our TypeScript SDK. Error observed: "expected 2048 got 1024". They say this started after swapping to model "embed-large-v2" yesterday.

leo_support: repro snippets they sent (sanitized):
```ts
// ts client v0.8.7
import { Redwood } from 'redwood-sdk';
const c = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const v = new Array(1024).fill(0.123);
c.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-large-v2', input: [v] })
  .then(r => console.log('ok', r))
  .catch(e => console.error('err', e.message));
```

leo_support: they also tried python and go wrappers. Python call returns same mismatch. Curl against REST returns fine (2048 dim) which is confusing.

tess_engineer: thanks. quick checklist: model catalog says embed-large-v2 -> vector_size 2048. If curl is fine, likely client serialization issue. TS SDK v0.8.7 had a node-stream/content-length edge-case; python had batch-flattening in older line. we should confirm exact SDK versions and whether they used a single vector (batch size 1) or a nested batch.

sam_platform: logged trace id a-8c7e. I pulled server logs for that trace: server received JSON with "input": [0.0,0.0,...] (1-D array) for some requests, and for others it got an array-of-arrays. When the 1-D payload came in, server validation throws "dimension mismatch expected 2048 got 1024". So the server is doing shape inference and rejecting.

leo_support: customer confirms they are passing input: [vector] (batch of one) in their code. They attach package.json and go.mod showing mixed SDKs: ts-sdk@0.8.7, python-sdk==0.10.0, go-sdk v0.7.1.

anu_devex: suggested immediate mitigations for the customer: 1) wrap their vector in an extra bracket (input=[[...]]), 2) call the REST API as a temporary workaround, 3) pin to ts-sdk@0.8.9+ or python sdk >=0.10.2 (patches rolling). Also ask them to test sending two vectors (batch size 2) to see if serialization differs.

tess_engineer: dug in locally. Repro for python: python-sdk 0.10.0 flattens batch-of-one arrays when the inner list looks like numbers -> sends 1-D array. Fix is to ensure we serialize lists of numbers as nested arrays if the user passed a single vector inside a list. I have a unit test failing. Patch will be cherry-picked to 0.10.x and main.

sam_platform: ts-sdk issue: when sending large requests with node streams we compute Content-Length incorrectly for some gzip-on-the-fly paths which made node chunk the body; in unlucky timing the server saw a truncated JSON that parsed as 1-D array. PR opened to enforce Buffer accumulation before header set.

leo_support: customer additionally sees intermittent 429s when they try to batch >3000 vectors in one request and timeouts in Go when request duration >60s. They asked for recommended chunking and retry algorithm.

anu_devex: recommended guidance to include to customer:
- chunk vectors to 400-800 per request for embed-large-v2 (monitor token/byte size if vectors are dense)
- implement exponential backoff with jitter: base = 0.15s, multiplier = 2, maxDelay = 8s, maxRetries = 6, jitter = uniform(-0.1 * delay, +0.1 * delay)
- on HTTP 429/503 retry; on 4xx (other than 429) do not retry automatically
- increase client socket timeout for bulk jobs (e.g., requests timeout=180s or Go context deadline accordingly)
- consider Redwood Dedicated for sustained high throughput to avoid 429s from shared pools

tess_engineer: server-side improvement planned: make validation error explicit when array shape mismatches, e.g. "received 1-D vector length 1024; model embed-large-v2 expects 2048 dims; if sending batch, provide nested arrays [[...]]". Filing INF-511.

sam_platform: release plan: python patch release 0.10.2 today (fix flattening), ts patch 0.8.9 (Content-Length fix) staged, go SDK change queued for v0.7.2. I'll coordinate with releases.

devops_bot: ci pipeline started - python-sdk 0.10.2 build #2219, ts-sdk 0.8.9 build #3347

leo_support: the customer tested wrapping with input=[[...]] and that immediately fixed the mismatch. they asked for ETA for official patch.

tess_engineer: ETA: python 0.10.2 in ~1.5 hours assuming CI passes. ts 0.8.9 in ~3 hours (longer because of node test flakiness). I'll post the pip/npm upgrade snippets here when live.

anu_devex: drafting reply to customer (to be short):
- root cause: SDKs serialized batch-of-one inconsistently leading server to see a raw 1-D vector (1024) instead of nested 2048 vector -> dimension mismatch.
- immediate workaround: wrap vector in another list (input=[[...]]) or call REST / use curl.
- short-term: upgrade python to 0.10.2 and ts to 0.8.9 when available.
- for throughput: chunk requests and implement backoff + bump client timeouts or request Dedicated capacity.

ci_bot: python-sdk 0.10.2 build #2219 passed tests and is publishing to PyPI.

devops_bot: ts-sdk 0.8.9 npm publish scheduled after artifact verification.

tess_engineer: published: pip install --upgrade redwood-sdk==0.10.2 and npm i @redwood/sdk@0.8.9. changelog: "Fix: embeddings serialization for single-vector batches (preserve nested arrays). Fix: node stream Content-Length for large batch uploads."

leo_support: forwarded pip/npm upgrade to Acme, they verified python upgrade fixed their python calls and ts upgrade fixed their node truncation/timeout issues. they still plan to chunk large jobs.

sam_platform: follow-ups: 1) add FAQ line in docs about embedding dims and sample curl + nested array examples, 2) add server-side guard to reject unambiguous truncated JSON earlier with a clear message, 3) monitor support queue for similar tickets and correlate SDK versions.

anu_devex: I'll update support KB and include the recommended backoff snippet and chunking guidelines.

leo_support: closing loop with customer. thanks team. :thumbsup:

last activity note: tess_engineer posted release notes and pip/npm instructions at 1780057890
